chk_problem.reason: Both drafts identify the high computational cost and energy consumption of running video object detectors on edge devices as the core problem.

chk_method.reason: Both drafts describe the ALBIREO framework and its key components: Kalman filter uncertainty, a rescue mechanism, and empty-scene screening.

chk_data.reason: Both drafts identify the exact same dataset: the BDD100K multi-object tracking validation split with 200 clips and 7 classes.

chk_setup.reason: Both drafts list the same hardware platforms (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor and AGX Orin) and detectors (YOLO11x, YOLO26x, RF-DETR-Large).

chk_primary_result.reason: Draft A presents the overall performance range across all configurations as the primary result, whereas Draft B focuses on the specific numbers for the YOLO26x configuration.

chk_secondary_result.reason: Draft A highlights the YOLO26x configuration results, while Draft B highlights the AP@50–EDP Pareto frontier over the baselines.

chk_baseline.reason: Both drafts list the same set of baselines, with Draft A being slightly more detailed by explicitly mentioning vanilla per-frame inference.

chk_conclusion.reason: Both drafts conclude that ALBIREO serves as a practical drop-in efficiency layer for edge video detection pipelines.

chk_limitation.reason: Both drafts identify the drift of Kalman dynamics under erratic motion as a limitation, with Draft B mentioning an additional domain-dependency limitation.
